## [18] Towards climate-ready fisheries management in the Northeast Atlantic and Mediterranean Sea
<hr />

{{< fa calendar-days >}}&nbsp; June 2026
<br/>{{< fa user >}}&nbsp; **Arnaud Auber** (IFREMER, France) 
<br/>{{< fa globe >}}&nbsp; [MAESTRO](https://www.fondationbiodiversite.fr/en/the-frb-in-action/programs-and-projects/le-cesab/maestro/) project

<br/>

**Abstract**

Oceans provide more than 60% of the world’s monetized ecosystem services and are 
essential for food security and economic activity through marine resources such 
as fish and benthic invertebrates. Yet climate change and fishing pressure are 
altering the distribution, abundance, and composition of marine species worldwide. 
Although many studies have projected future species distributions, far less 
attention has been devoted to understanding how these drivers affect the functional 
diversity of marine communities, a key determinant of ecosystem functioning. 
This gap limits our ability to anticipate the combined impacts of climate change 
and fisheries exploitation and to develop adaptive management strategies. The 
[MAESTRO](https://www.fondationbiodiversite.fr/en/the-frb-in-action/programs-and-projects/le-cesab/maestro/) project addresses this challenge by integrating datasets on fish and 
invertebrate communities from the Northeast Atlantic and the Mediterranean Sea. 
Its first objective is to quantify the effects of climate change and fishing on 
the functional diversity of communities over the past three decades. The second 
objective is to predict how these communities will respond to ocean warming from 
the contemporary period to the end of the century. Finally, [MAESTRO](https://www.fondationbiodiversite.fr/en/the-frb-in-action/programs-and-projects/le-cesab/maestro/) seeks to 
identify alternative fishing strategies targeting novel combinations of species 
that minimize impacts on ecosystem functioning while maintaining levels of 
fishery landings, supporting climate-resilient fisheries management.
